title: Go Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: main is where this Go program starts. fmt.Println prints values on a new line.
notes: Keep package main and func main in a runnable program.

entries.name: Name a number
entries.summary: The := sign makes a new local variable and chooses its type from the value.
notes: Use = to change an existing variable; := declares a new one.

entries.name: Use a clear type
entries.summary: A type says what kind of value fits a variable. int stores whole numbers.
notes: An int cannot store text like "eight".

entries.name: Choose a path
entries.summary: if checks a true-or-false rule. Go uses braces around the steps.
notes: Put the opening brace on the if line.

entries.name: Repeat steps
entries.summary: A for loop can count from a start value until a test becomes false.
notes: Check whether your last number should use < or <=.

entries.name: Keep a growing list
entries.summary: A slice is a view of a list of values. append returns a slice with more items.
notes: Keep the slice returned by append.

entries.name: Visit list values
entries.summary: range gives an index and a value for each slice item. _ ignores the index.
notes: A single range variable is the index, not the value.

entries.name: Look up a key
entries.summary: A map links a key to a value. The key below is a name and the value is a count.
notes: Check the second lookup result when you need to know if a key exists.

entries.name: Use a small function
entries.summary: A function can take a number and return a number. This example stores a function in twice.
notes: Write the return type after the input list.

entries.name: Group related fields
entries.summary: A struct groups named fields. Here a book has one title and one page count.
notes: Exported field names begin with a capital letter.

entries.name: Change an original value
entries.summary: A pointer stores an address. & gets an address, and * reaches the value there.

example.code:
package main
import "fmt"
func main() {
score := 3
place := &score
*place = 7
fmt.Println(score)
}

notes: Do not read through a nil pointer.

entries.name: Pass a value through a channel
entries.summary: A channel carries values between parts of a program. A buffered channel can hold one value here.

example.code:
package main
import "fmt"
func main() {
scores := make(chan int, 1)
scores <- 8
fmt.Println(<-scores)
}

notes: An unbuffered send needs a receiver ready, or it will wait.
